This export does not re-derive or assert exact metrics for this run -- validate_deployment_artifacts.py instead checks that the reloaded model's PREDICTIONS match this run's original in-memory predictions, which is the relevant guarantee for deployment fidelity.
Same caveat as above -- see validate_deployment_artifacts.py for the actual deployment-fidelity check performed.

source_of_truth: reconstruct.py, executed unmodified via runpy.run_path() by this script. No hyperparameters, features, splits, or modeling logic were changed, approximated, or reimplemented to produce this export.
training_data_assumptions: M5 competition retail sales data, FOODS category, store CA_1.
Chronological train/test split at CUTOFF with an expiry embargo (train batches' expiry_date < CUTOFF <= test batches' received_date) to prevent leakage between train and test.
current_inventory is defined as qty_received at received_date -- no mid-life inventory tracking exists in the source data.

required_input_schema_for_new_inference.note: The engineered fields require the full historical M5 item-daily sales/calendar/price long table to compute trailing windows and cumulative SNAP/event counts. This is the same limitation already documented in the web application's Data Input page: arbitrary new company data cannot be scored end-to-end without either (a) equivalent historical sales history for the same items, or (b) a redesigned feature set that doesn't require it. This export does not change or solve that limitation -- it only makes the existing, already-trained models reusable without retraining.
